chapters.title: The Tribes and the Land Left Untaken
chapters.html:
Judges 1

Judah Goes Up First

1And it came to pass after the death of Joshua that the sons of Israel asked the LORD, "Who shall go up first for us against the Canaanites, to fight against them?"

2The LORD said, "Judah shall go up. I have given the land into his hand."

3Judah said to Simeon his brother, "Come up with me into my lot, and let us fight against the Canaanites, and I too will go with you into your lot." So Simeon went with him.

4Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they struck ten thousand men at Bezek.

5They found Adoni-bezek at Bezek and fought against him, and they struck the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

6Adoni-bezek fled, and they pursued him, caught him and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

7Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and their big toes cut off used to gather scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me." They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

8The sons of Judah fought against Jerusalem and took it. They struck it with the sword and set the city on fire.

9Afterward the sons of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev and the lowland.

10Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron — the name of Hebron before was Kiriath-arba — and they struck Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai.

Othniel and Achsah

11From there they went against the inhabitants of Debir. The name of Debir before was Kiriath-sepher.

12Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and takes it, I will give him Achsah my daughter as a wife."

13Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it, and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.

14And it came to pass, when she came to him, that she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"

15She said to him, "Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

Judah and Simeon

16The sons of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up with the sons of Judah from the city of palm trees into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the Negev of Arad, and they went and lived with the people.

17Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who lived in Zephath and devoted it to destruction. So the name of the city was called Hormah.

18Judah took Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory and Ekron with its territory.

19The LORD was with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country, but he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

20They gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.

21But the sons of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, and the Jebusites have lived with the sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.

The House of Joseph

22The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.

23The house of Joseph sent spies to Bethel. The name of the city before was Luz.

24The watchmen saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Please show us the way into the city, and we will deal with you in loyal love."

25He showed them the way into the city, and they struck the city with the sword, but they let the man and all his family go.

26The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city and called its name Luz. That is its name to this day.

The Canaanites Who Remained

27Manasseh did not drive out Beth-shean and its towns, or Taanach and its towns, or the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, or the inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, or the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns, for the Canaanites were determined to live in that land.

28And it came to pass, when Israel grew strong, that they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but did not drive them out completely.

29Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, and the Canaanites lived among them in Gezer.

30Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol, and the Canaanites lived among them and became forced labor.

31Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco or the inhabitants of Sidon, or of Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik or Rehob.

32The Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they did not drive them out.

33Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-anath, and they lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land. The inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced labor for them.

34The Amorites pressed the sons of Dan back into the hill country, for they did not let them come down into the valley.

35The Amorites were determined to live in Mount Heres, in Aijalon and in Shaalbim, but the hand of the house of Joseph weighed heavy on them, and they became forced labor.

36The border of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.

Notes

  • v1 "after the death of Joshua" — Joshua opens after the death of Moses (Joshua 1:1). The two books begin the same way, and the difference is the point: Moses had a successor, Joshua has none. Israel asks the LORD instead, and the answer is a tribe, not a man.

  • v7 "As I have done, so God has repaid me" — shillam, the verb of payment and of shalom, being whole. The one foreign king in the chapter who speaks names God's justice in his own punishment.

  • v8 "took it… set the city on fire" — but v21 says the Jebusites stayed in Jerusalem, and Joshua 15:63 says Judah could not drive them out. The city is taken and burned here and still not held; it becomes Israel's only when David takes it (2 Samuel 5:6–7).

  • vv10–15 — told almost word for word in Joshua 15:14–19. Here the text adds that Othniel is Caleb's younger brother, ha-qatan mimmennu, as it does again at 3:9. The words can also be read of Kenaz, which would make Othniel Caleb's nephew; the Hebrew allows both.

  • v16 "the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law" — choten Moshe, the family of Hobab (4:11). The city of palm trees is Jericho (Deuteronomy 34:3). The Greek calls them the sons of Jothor, that is, Jethro.

  • v17 "devoted it to destruction… Hormah" — va-yacharimu, from cherem; Hormah is from the same root. The same wordplay names the place in Numbers 21:3.

  • v18 "Judah took Gaza… Ashkelon… Ekron" — the Greek says the opposite: Judah did not inherit Gaza or its territory, and adds Ashdod to the list. The Hebrew stands, but the rest of the book backs the Greek: v19 says Judah could not take the valley, 3:3 lists the five lords of the Philistines among the nations left, and Samson finds Gaza Philistine (16:1).

  • v19 "he could not drive out" — the Hebrew has only not to drive out, with no could. The verb is supplied, as every translation supplies it. The Greek has because Rechab set them apart, reading rekhev, chariots, as a name.

  • v24 "we will deal with you in loyal love" — chesed, the promise the spies made to Rahab (Joshua 2:14). Rahab stayed in Israel; this man leaves and builds a new Luz.

  • vv27–36 did not drive out — the refrain of the chapter, tribe after tribe, moving north and ending with Dan pushed back into the hills. Deuteronomy 7:2 had said You shall make no covenant with them; here they become forced labor (v28, as Joshua 17:13) and live among Israel. Chapter 2 gives the LORD's answer.

chapters.title: Bochim, and the Pattern of the Judges
chapters.html:
Judges 2

The Messenger at Bochim

1The messenger of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land that I swore to your fathers. I said, 'I will never break My covenant with you,

2and as for you, you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall tear down their altars.' But you have not listened to My voice. What is this you have done?

3So I also said, 'I will not drive them out before you. They will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.'"

4And it came to pass, when the messenger of the LORD spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, that the people lifted up their voices and wept.

5They called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.

A Generation That Did Not Know the LORD

6When Joshua had sent the people away, the sons of Israel went each to his inheritance to take possession of the land.

7The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work the LORD had done for Israel.

8Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, a hundred and ten years old.

9They buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

10All that generation also were gathered to their fathers, and another generation rose after them who did not know the LORD or the work He had done for Israel.

The Pattern

11The sons of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals.

12They forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and went after other gods, from the gods of the peoples around them, and bowed down to them, and provoked the LORD to anger.

13They forsook the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.

14The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He gave them into the hand of raiders who plundered them. He sold them into the hand of their enemies all around, and they could no longer stand before their enemies.

15Wherever they went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for harm, as the LORD had said and as the LORD had sworn to them, and they were in great distress.

16Then the LORD raised up judges, and they saved them from the hand of those who plundered them.

17Yet they did not listen even to their judges, for they prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way their fathers had walked, obeying the commandments of the LORD; they did not do so.

18Whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge, for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning because of those who oppressed and crushed them.

19And it would come to pass, when the judge died, that they turned back and acted more corruptly than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They did not let go of any of their deeds or their stubborn ways.

Nations Left to Test Israel

20The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He said, "Because this nation has transgressed My covenant that I commanded their fathers and has not listened to My voice,

21I too will no longer drive out before them any of the nations that Joshua left when he died,

22in order to test Israel by them, whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their fathers kept it, or not."

23So the LORD left those nations, not driving them out quickly, and He did not give them into the hand of Joshua.

Notes

  • v1 "the messenger of the LORD" — mal'akh YHWH, as in Genesis 16:7 and Exodus 3:2. He speaks in the first person as God: I brought you up… My covenant. Bochim means weepers, and v5 names the place for what the people do there. The Greek adds that he went up to Bethel and to the house of Israel.

  • v3 "thorns in your sides" — the Hebrew has only le-tsiddim, for sides. Thorns is supplied from the warning this repeats: Numbers 33:55, thorns in your sides, and Joshua 23:13. The Greek has for afflictions.

  • vv6–9 — these verses repeat Joshua 24:28–31 almost word for word, taking up the story again from Joshua's death before the book goes on. Here the burial place is Timnath-heres, portion of the sun; Joshua 19:50 and 24:30 have Timnath-serah, the same letters with the last two reversed.

  • v10 "who did not know the LORD" — lo yad'u: not that they had never heard of Him, but that they had not seen what He did. v7 says the elders had seen all the great work. The work was not passed on.

  • v11 "did evil in the eyes of the LORD" — the refrain of the book, which returns at the start of each judge's story (3:7, 3:12, 4:1, 6:1, 10:6, 13:1). The Baals, ha-be'alim, is plural: the local Baals of many towns. Ba'al is the common word for owner, master, husband.

  • v13 "Baal and the Ashtaroth" — Ashtaroth is the plural of Ashtoreth, the goddess worshipped beside Baal.

  • v16 "judges" — shofetim. The verb shafat covers ruling and setting right as well as deciding cases, and v16 says what these judges do: they saved them. The book's judges are deliverers first; only Deborah is shown hearing cases (4:5).

  • v18 "the LORD was moved to pity" — yinnachem, the verb of Exodus 32:14, the LORD relented. Here what moves Him is their groaning, na'aqatam, the word used of Israel groaning in Egypt (Exodus 2:24).

  • v19 "their stubborn ways" — darkam ha-qashah, their hard way, from the same root as the stiff-necked people of Exodus 32:9.

  • vv21–23 — the land left untaken in chapter 1 is explained three ways in this book: as punishment (v3, v21), as a test (v22, 3:4) and as training for war (3:2).

chapters.title: Othniel, Ehud and Shamgar
chapters.html:
Judges 3

The Nations Left in the Land

1These are the nations the LORD left in order to test Israel by them, all those who had not known any of the wars of Canaan —

2only so that the generations of the sons of Israel might know war, to teach it to those who had not known it before:

3the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the hill country of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.

4They were there to test Israel by them, to know whether they would obey the commandments of the LORD, which He commanded their fathers through Moses.

5So the sons of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.

6They took their daughters for themselves as wives, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.

Othniel

7The sons of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.

8The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.

9The sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for the sons of Israel, who saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.

10The spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.

11The land had rest forty years, and Othniel son of Kenaz died.

Ehud

12The sons of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the eyes of the LORD.

13He gathered to himself the sons of Ammon and Amalek, went and struck Israel, and they took possession of the city of palm trees.

14The sons of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

15The sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them, Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The sons of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon king of Moab.

16Ehud made himself a sword with two edges, a cubit long, and he strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh.

17He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon was a very fat man.

18And it came to pass, when he had finished presenting the tribute, that he sent away the people who had carried it.

19But he himself turned back at the carved images near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret word for you, O king." The king said, "Silence!" All who stood by him went out from him.

20Ehud came to him as he was sitting alone in his cool upper room. Ehud said, "I have a word from God for you," and the king rose from his seat.

21Ehud reached out his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh and thrust it into his belly.

22The hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the dung came out.

23Ehud went out through the porch, shut the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them.

24When he had gone out, the king's servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked, and they said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool room."

25They waited until they were ashamed, but he still did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened them, and there lay their lord, fallen to the ground, dead.

26Ehud escaped while they delayed. He passed the carved images and escaped to Seirah.

27And it came to pass, when he arrived, that he blew the horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, with him at their head.

28He said to them, "Follow me, for the LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand." They went down after him and seized the fords of the Jordan against Moab, and let no one cross.

29At that time they struck about ten thousand men of Moab, all of them stout and all of them strong men, and not one escaped.

30So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest eighty years.

Shamgar

31After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad. He too saved Israel.

Notes

  • v7 "the Baals and the Asherahs" — ha-asherot, a feminine plural, set beside the Baals as the Ashtaroth are in 2:13. The more common asherim are the sacred poles of Deuteronomy 16:21; here the word names the goddesses themselves.

  • v8 "Cushan-rishathaim" — the second half of the name is double wickedness, rish'atayim. Whether it is his name or what Israel called him, the text does not say. Aram-naharaim, Aram of the two rivers, is where Abraham's servant found Rebekah (Genesis 24:10).

  • v9 "a deliverer… who saved them" — moshia, from yasha, to save, the root of the name Joshua. Othniel is the one judge whose story has nothing in it but the pattern of chapter 2: sin, sale, cry, deliverer, rest.

  • v15 "a left-handed man" — ish itter yad-yemino, a man bound in his right hand. He is a Ben-Yemini, a Benjaminite, a son of the right hand, and his right hand is the one he does not use. Judges 20:16 counts seven hundred left-handed slingers in Benjamin.

  • vv15, 17, 18 "tribute" — minchah, the word for the grain offering in Leviticus 2. Israel's gift to the king of Moab is the word for a gift to God.

  • v16 "a cubit long" — gomed, a measure found only here. Its length is unknown; cubit is the usual guess, a short blade that can hide on the thigh.

  • vv19–20 "a secret word… a word from God" — davar is both word and thing. Ehud has a davar for the king, and what he gives him is the sword. Silence! is has, a single syllable, and the room empties.

  • vv22–24 "the dung came out… relieving himself" — ha-parshedonah in v22 and ha-misderonah in v23 are both found only here, and their meanings are argued; the dung and the porch are the usual readings. In v24 the servants say he is covering his feet, the Hebrew way of saying a man is relieving himself (so also 1 Samuel 24:3). The Greek does not have the last clause of v22.

  • v29 "all of them stout" — kol shamen, every fat one, the Moabite soldiers described with the word for their fat king's body (v17 has bari, the fat cows of Genesis 41:2).

  • v31 "Shamgar son of Anath… an oxgoad" — Anath is the name of a Canaanite goddess, and Shamgar is named again in the Song of Deborah (5:6). He fights with a farmer's tool, like Samson's jawbone (15:15).

The spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
The land had rest forty years, and Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Ehud
The sons of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the eyes of the LORD.
He gathered to himself the sons of Ammon and Amalek, went and struck Israel, and they took possession of the city of palm trees.
The sons of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

The sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them, Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The sons of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud made himself a sword with two edges, a cubit long, and he strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh.
He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon was a very fat man.
And it came to pass, when he had finished presenting the tribute, that he sent away the people who had carried it.
But he himself turned back at the carved images near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret word for you, O king." The king said, "Silence!" All who stood by him went out from him.
Ehud came to him as he was sitting alone in his cool upper room. Ehud said, "I have a word from God for you," and the king rose from his seat.
Ehud reached out his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh and thrust it into his belly.
The hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the dung came out.
Ehud went out through the porch, shut the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them.
When he had gone out, the king's servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked, and they said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool room."
They waited until they were ashamed, but he still did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened them, and there lay their lord, fallen to the ground, dead.
Ehud escaped while they delayed. He passed the carved images and escaped to Seirah.
And it came to pass, when he arrived, that he blew the horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, with him at their head.
He said to them, "Follow me, for the LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand." They went down after him and seized the fords of the Jordan against Moab, and let no one cross.
At that time they struck about ten thousand men of Moab, all of them stout and all of them strong men, and not one escaped.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest eighty years.
Shamgar
After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad. He too saved Israel.

chapters.title: Deborah, Barak and Jael
chapters.html:
Judges 4

Deborah

1The sons of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD after Ehud died.

2The LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.

3The sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he had oppressed the sons of Israel harshly for twenty years.

4Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.

5She used to sit under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went up to her for judgment.

6She sent and called Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, and said to him, "Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded, 'Go, march to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from the sons of Naphtali and the sons of Zebulun?

7I will draw out Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, to meet you at the Kishon River, with his chariots and his troops, and I will give him into your hand.'"

8Barak said to her, "If you will go with me, I will go, but if you will not go with me, I will not go."

9She said, "I will certainly go with you. But the road you are taking will not lead to your glory, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh.

10Barak called out Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up behind him, and Deborah went up with him.

11Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the sons of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far away as the oak in Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.

The Battle at the Kishon

12They told Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.

13Sisera called out all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon River.

14Deborah said to Barak, "Up! For this is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him.

15The LORD threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into panic before Barak with the sword, and Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.

16Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and the whole army of Sisera fell by the sword; not one was left.

Jael

17Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

18Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me. Do not be afraid." So he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.

19He said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink and covered him.

20He said to her, "Stand at the entrance of the tent. And it shall come to pass, if anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?', that you shall say, 'No.'"

21But Jael the wife of Heber took a tent peg, took the hammer in her hand, went to him quietly and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground. He was fast asleep and exhausted, and he died.

22Just then Barak came, pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man you are looking for." He went in with her, and there lay Sisera, fallen dead, with the peg in his temple.

23So on that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the sons of Israel.

24The hand of the sons of Israel pressed harder and harder on Jabin king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.

Notes

  • v2 "Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor" — Joshua defeated a Jabin king of Hazor and burned the city (Joshua 11:1, 10–11). A second Jabin reigns there again; the name may have been carried by the kings of Hazor.

  • v4 "Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth" — ishah nevi'ah eshet Lappidot. Deborah means bee. Eshet Lappidot is usually read as the wife of Lappidoth, but lappid is a torch (the torch of fire of Genesis 15:17), and the phrase can also mean a woman of torches, a fiery woman. No husband is mentioned again. The Hebrew allows both; the text follows the usual reading.

  • vv6–7 "march… I will draw out Sisera" — mashakhta… u-mashakhti, the same verb, draw, used of both sides: Barak draws his men to Tabor, and the LORD draws Sisera to the river.

  • v8 "If you will go with me, I will go" — the Greek adds Barak's reason: for I do not know the day on which the LORD gives success to His messenger with me. Hebrews 11:32 names Barak among the people of faith.

  • v9 "into the hand of a woman" — Barak, and any reader, will think of Deborah. The woman turns out to be Jael (v21).

  • v11 "Heber the Kenite" — a Kenite clan that moved north, away from the Kenites in Judah (1:16). Heber is from the root to join, and v17 gives what he had joined: peace with Jabin. The note in v11 is there to explain v17.

  • v15 "The LORD threw Sisera… into panic" — va-yahom, the verb of Exodus 14:24, where the LORD threw the camp of Egypt into panic at the sea. Here too the chariots are ruined by water: the Song of Deborah says the torrent of Kishon swept them away (5:21).

  • v20 "Is there a man here?… No" — ha-yesh poh ish… ayin. He means a man hiding; the answer is truer than he knows. The one who will kill him is not a man.

  • v21 "He was fast asleep and exhausted" — nirdam va-ya'af. Nirdam is from the root of tardemah, the deep sleep that fell on the human in Genesis 2:21. Va-ya'af is either was weary (from ayef) or fainted, flew away; the Greek reads he was stunned and darkened.

  • v24 "pressed harder and harder" — halokh ve-qashah, going and being hard, the way Hebrew says a thing grows steadily. Chapter 5 tells the same victory as a song.

chapters.title: The Song of Deborah
chapters.html:
Judges 5

The Song of Deborah and Barak

1Then Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang on that day:

2When locks hang loose in Israel,
when the people offer themselves willingly —
bless the LORD!

3Hear, you kings; give ear, you rulers:
I, to the LORD I will sing;
I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.

4LORD, when You went out from Seir,
when You marched from the field of Edom,
the earth shook, the heavens poured,
the clouds poured down water.

5The mountains flowed down before the LORD,
the One of Sinai,
before the LORD, the God of Israel.

6In the days of Shamgar son of Anath,
in the days of Jael, the roads were empty,
and those who went on their way
went by winding paths.

7The villagers were gone in Israel, they were gone,
until I arose, Deborah,
until I arose, a mother in Israel.

8They chose new gods;
then war was at the gates.
Was a shield to be seen, or a spear,
among forty thousand in Israel?

9My heart is with the commanders of Israel,
who offered themselves willingly among the people.
Bless the LORD!

10You who ride on white donkeys,
you who sit on saddle-rugs,
and you who walk on the road — tell of it!

11Over the voice of the singers at the watering places,
there they recount the righteous acts of the LORD,
the righteous acts for His villagers in Israel.
Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.

Awake, Deborah

12Awake, awake, Deborah!
Awake, awake, sing a song!
Arise, Barak, and lead away your captives,
son of Abinoam!

13Then a remnant went down to the nobles, the people;
the LORD went down for me against the mighty.

14From Ephraim came those whose root is in Amalek;
after you, Benjamin, with your kinsmen;
from Machir came down commanders,
and from Zebulun those who carry the scribe's staff.

15The princes of Issachar were with Deborah;
as Issachar was, so was Barak,
sent into the valley at his heels.
Among the clans of Reuben
great were the resolves of heart.

16Why did you sit among the sheepfolds,
to hear the piping for the flocks?
Among the clans of Reuben
great were the searchings of heart.

17Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan;
and Dan, why does he live as a guest by the ships?
Asher sat at the shore of the sea
and stayed by his landings.

18Zebulun is a people that scorned death with their lives,
and Naphtali on the heights of the field.

The Stars Fought

19Kings came, they fought;
then the kings of Canaan fought
at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo.
They took no silver for spoil.

20From heaven the stars fought;
from their courses they fought against Sisera.

21The torrent of Kishon swept them away,
the ancient torrent, the torrent of Kishon.
March on, my soul, with strength!

22Then the horses' hooves hammered
with the galloping, galloping of his stallions.

23'Curse Meroz,' said the messenger of the LORD,
'curse its inhabitants utterly,
because they did not come to the help of the LORD,
to the help of the LORD against the mighty.'

Jael

24Most blessed of women be Jael,
the wife of Heber the Kenite;
of women in the tent most blessed.

25He asked for water; she gave him milk.
In a bowl fit for nobles she brought him curds.

26Her hand she put to the tent peg,
her right hand to the workmen's hammer.
She hammered Sisera, she crushed his head;
she shattered and pierced his temple.

27Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay;
between her feet he sank, he fell;
where he sank, there he fell, destroyed.

Sisera's Mother

28Through the window she looked down and wailed,
Sisera's mother, through the lattice:
'Why is his chariot so slow in coming?
Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots delay?'

29The wisest of her ladies answer her;
she, too, gives herself the answer:

30'Are they not finding and dividing the spoil?
A womb, two wombs for every man;
spoil of dyed cloth for Sisera,
spoil of dyed cloth, embroidered,
dyed cloth, two embroidered pieces
for the necks of the spoil.'

31So may all Your enemies perish, LORD!
But may those who love Him be like the sun
when it goes out in its might.
The land had rest forty years.

Notes

  • v2 "When locks hang loose in Israel" — bi-fro'a pera'ot, a verb with its own noun. Pera is long, uncut hair: the Nazirite lets the locks of the hair of his head grow long (Numbers 6:5), and Deuteronomy 32:42 has the long-haired heads of the enemy. Read this way, the song opens with fighters under a vow, their hair uncut. Older English reads when leaders lead; the Greek has a revelation was revealed, taking the verb as uncover.

  • v5 "The mountains flowed down… the One of Sinai" — harim nazelu, from nazal, to flow, the word for the flowing waters of Exodus 15:8. The Greek has were shaken, reading nazollu, quaked, the form in Isaiah 64:1 (Hebrew 63:19), the mountains quaked at Your presence. Zeh Sinai is this Sinai; the same two words stand after God in Psalm 68:8, and there, as here, they read as a title: the God who met Israel at Sinai.

  • vv7, 11 "the villagers… His villagers" — perazon, found only in this song, from perazot, unwalled villages (Ezekiel 38:11). The open country emptied until Deborah arose. The Greek reads the mighty. Until I arose is shaqqamti, which may be I arose or an old form of you arose; the Greek has until Deborah arose.

  • vv15–16 "resolves of heart… searchings of heart" — chiqqei lev, then chiqrei lev: one letter changes. Reuben made great resolutions, then great deliberations, and stayed with the sheep.

  • v17 "why does he live as a guest by the ships?" — yagur, the verb of the ger, the guest. Dan's first lot ran to the coast opposite Joppa (Joshua 19:46); the song asks why a tribe of Israel stayed by the ships, living like a guest.

  • vv20–21 "the stars fought… the torrent of Kishon swept them away" — the prose of 4:15 says only that the LORD threw Sisera… into panic. The song says how: heaven fought, and the river rose over the chariots. The ancient torrent, nachal qedumim, is also read the onrushing torrent; the Greek has torrent of the ancients.

  • v24 "Most blessed of women be Jael" — the Greek is eulogētheiē en gynaixin, blessed among women. Elizabeth greets Mary with the same words in Luke 1:42, Eulogēmenē sy en gynaixin.

  • vv26–27 "She hammered Sisera… between her feet he sank" — the prose of 4:21 has him asleep when the peg goes in; the song has him fall at her feet. The two tellings are set side by side and neither is adjusted to the other. The Greek has her left hand to the peg.

  • v28 "wailed" — va-teyabbev, found only here. His mother waits at the window, as the reader knows he is dead.

  • v30 "A womb, two wombs for every man" — racham rachamatayim. Racham is the plain word for womb, and she uses it of the captured girls. The song lets her say it and does not comment. For the necks of the spoil is hard: most read it for my neck, as spoil.

chapters.title: The Call of Gideon
chapters.html:
Judges 6

Midian

1The sons of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian seven years.

2The hand of Midian prevailed over Israel. Because of Midian the sons of Israel made for themselves the dens in the mountains, the caves and the strongholds.

3And it would come to pass, whenever Israel had sown, that Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east would come up and attack them.

4They would camp against them and destroy the produce of the land as far as Gaza, and leave no food in Israel, and no sheep or ox or donkey.

5For they would come up with their livestock and their tents, and come like locusts for number; they and their camels could not be counted. They came into the land to ruin it.

6Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD.

A Prophet

7And it came to pass, when the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD because of Midian,

8that the LORD sent a prophet to the sons of Israel, and he said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out of the house of slaves.

9I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you, and drove them out before you and gave you their land.

10I said to you, "I am the LORD your God. Do not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live." But you have not listened to My voice.'"

The Messenger at Ophrah

11The messenger of the LORD came and sat under the terebinth at Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, while Gideon his son was beating out wheat in the winepress, to hide it from Midian.

12The messenger of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, "The LORD is with you, mighty man of valor."

13Gideon said to him, "Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this found us? Where are all His wonders that our fathers told us of, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?' But now the LORD has abandoned us and given us into the hand of Midian."

14The LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?"

15He said to Him, "Please, my Lord, how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."

16The LORD said to him, "Because I will be with you, you shall strike Midian as one man."

17He said to Him, "If I have found favor in Your eyes, give me a sign that it is You who are speaking with me.

18Please do not go away from here until I come back to You and bring out my offering and set it before You." He said, "I will stay until you come back."

19Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, and brought them out to him under the terebinth and presented them.

20The messenger of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened bread, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth." He did so.

21The messenger of the LORD reached out the tip of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread, and fire went up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. Then the messenger of the LORD went from his sight.

22Gideon saw that he was the messenger of the LORD, and Gideon said, "Alas, Lord GOD! For I have seen the messenger of the LORD face to face."

23The LORD said to him, "Peace to you. Do not be afraid; you shall not die."

24Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it The LORD Is Peace. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

The Altar of Baal

25And it came to pass that night that the LORD said to him, "Take your father's bull, the second bull, seven years old. Tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the sacred pole beside it.

26Build an altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold, with the stones laid in order. Then take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering with the wood of the sacred pole that you cut down."

27So Gideon took ten men from his servants and did as the LORD had told him. Because he was too afraid of his father's house and the men of the city to do it by day, he did it by night.

28When the men of the city rose early in the morning, the altar of Baal had been torn down, the sacred pole beside it had been cut down, and the second bull had been offered on the altar that had been built.

29They said to one another, "Who has done this?" They inquired and searched, and they said, "Gideon son of Joash has done this."

30The men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son, and he shall die, for he has torn down the altar of Baal and cut down the sacred pole beside it."

31But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you contend for Baal? Will you save him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because someone has torn down his altar."

32So on that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, meaning, "Let Baal contend against him, because he tore down his altar."

The Fleece

33All Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east gathered together, crossed over and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.

34The spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon, and he blew the horn, and the Abiezrites were called out to follow him.

35He sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and they too were called out to follow him. He sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.

36Gideon said to God, "If You will save Israel by my hand, as You have said,

37I am laying a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece only, and all the ground is dry, then I will know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You have said."

38It was so. He rose early the next morning and squeezed the fleece and wrung the dew out of it, a bowl full of water.

39Gideon said to God, "Do not let Your anger burn against me; let me speak just once more. Please let me make one more test with the fleece: let it be dry on the fleece only, and on all the ground let there be dew."

  • v2 "the dens in the mountains" — ha-minharot, found only here. Its root is uncertain, and dens, clefts in the rock, is the usual reading; the Greek has holes. Israel is driven into the rock to hide.

  • v11 "beating out wheat in the winepress" — wheat was threshed on an open floor where the wind could take the chaff. Gideon beats it in the pit of a winepress, where no one can see. The one the messenger calls mighty man of valor (v12) is hiding.

  • vv12–14 the messenger… The LORD turned to him — the messenger of the LORD speaks in v12, and in v14 the LORD turns to Gideon and speaks. As at the bush (Exodus 3:2–4), the text moves from the messenger to the LORD without explaining.

  • vv13, 15 "my lord… my Lord" — bi adoni, then bi Adonai. The consonants are the same; the vowels change from the word for a man of rank to the word used only of God, as in Moses' Please, my Lord (Exodus 4:10). Between v13 and v15, Gideon's guest has become the LORD.

  • v16 "Because I will be with you" — ki ehyeh immakh, word for word what God says to Moses at the bush (Exodus 3:12). Gideon, like Moses, has just said he is too small for the task.

  • v24 "The LORD Is Peace" — YHWH Shalom, answering the LORD's Peace to you in v23. It follows The LORD Will See (Genesis 22:14) and The LORD Is My Banner (Exodus 17:15), altars named for what the LORD did there.

  • v25 "the sacred pole" — ha-asherah, the wooden object for the goddess Asherah that Deuteronomy 16:21 forbids beside the LORD's altar. Here it stands beside Baal's altar, on the land of Gideon's father.

  • v32 "Jerubbaal" — Yerubba'al, let Baal contend, from riv, the verb of Joash's challenge in v31: If he is a god, let him contend for himself. The name is a dare, and Baal never answers it.

  • v34 "The spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon" — lavshah, put on, wore, the verb for putting on a garment. Gideon is not given the spirit; the spirit puts him on.

  • vv36–40 the fleece — Gideon asks for a sign twice, and the second test is the harder one, since a fleece naturally holds dew. A bowl full of water in v38 is sefel, the word used in the Song of Deborah for the bowl Jael brought to Sisera (5:25).

Midian

Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD.
A Prophet
And it came to pass, when the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD because of Midian,
that the LORD sent a prophet to the sons of Israel, and he said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out of the house of slaves.
I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you, and drove them out before you and gave you their land.

Gideon said to him, "Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this found us? Where are all His wonders that our fathers told us of, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?' But now the LORD has abandoned us and given us into the hand of Midian."
The LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
He said to Him, "Please, my Lord, how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
The LORD said to him, "Because I will be with you, you shall strike Midian as one man."
He said to Him, "If I have found favor in Your eyes, give me a sign that it is You who are speaking with me.

chapters.title: Gideon's Three Hundred
chapters.html:
Judges 7

Too Many

1Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, rose early with all the people who were with him and camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was north of him, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.

2The LORD said to Gideon, "The people with you are too many for Me to give Midian into their hand, or Israel will boast against Me, saying, 'My own hand has saved me.'

3And now proclaim in the hearing of the people, 'Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and leave Mount Gilead.'" Twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

4The LORD said to Gideon, "The people are still too many. Take them down to the water, and I will refine them for you there. And it shall come to pass that the one of whom I say to you, 'This one shall go with you,' shall go with you; and anyone of whom I say to you, 'This one shall not go with you,' shall not go."

5So he took the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, set him by himself; and everyone who kneels down to drink, set apart as well."

6The number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men, and all the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.

7The LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand. Let all the rest of the people go, each to his place."

8The three hundred took the people's provisions in their hands, and their horns. He sent all the rest of the men of Israel away, each to his tent, and kept the three hundred men. The camp of Midian was below him in the valley.

The Dream of the Barley Loaf

9And it came to pass that same night that the LORD said to him, "Rise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.

10But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,

11and you will hear what they are saying. Afterward your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down against the camp." So he went down with Purah his servant to the outposts of the men in ranks in the camp.

12Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the east lay along the valley like locusts for number, and their camels could not be counted, as many as the sand on the seashore.

13When Gideon came, a man was telling a dream to his friend. He said, "I had a dream: a round loaf of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midian. It came to the tent and struck it so that it fell, and turned it upside down, and the tent lay flat."

14His friend answered, "This is nothing else but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hand."

15And it came to pass, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, that he bowed down in worship. He returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Rise, for the LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hand."

Horns, Jars and Torches

16He divided the three hundred men into three companies and put horns into the hands of all of them, and empty jars, with torches inside the jars.

17He said to them, "Watch me and do the same. I am going to the edge of the camp, and it shall come to pass that as I do, so you shall do.

18When I blow the horn, I and all who are with me, you also blow the horns all around the camp, and say, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

19Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just posted the guards. They blew the horns and smashed the jars that were in their hands.

20The three companies blew the horns and broke the jars, held the torches in their left hands and the horns in their right hands to blow, and cried out, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"

21Each man stood in his place all around the camp, and the whole camp ran; they cried out and fled.

22When they blew the three hundred horns, the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow throughout the whole camp. The army fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the edge of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.

Oreb and Zeeb

23The men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.

24Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down against Midian and seize the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they seized the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

25They captured the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at the winepress of Zeeb, and they pursued Midian. They brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon beyond the Jordan.

Notes

  • vv1, 3 "the spring of Harod… afraid and trembling" — Charod and chared, trembling, from the same root. The army camps at Trembling Spring, and the first test sends the trembling home, as Deuteronomy 20:8 requires: Who is the man who is afraid and faint of heart? Let him go and return to his house.

  • v3 "leave Mount Gilead" — Gilead is east of the Jordan, and the camp is in the valley of Jezreel on the west. The verb, yitspor, is found only here, and its sense is guessed from the context. The place and the verb are both left as they stand; the Greek reads the same.

  • v4 "I will refine them" — etsrefennu, the verb for smelting metal to separate the pure from the dross. God tests the army the way a smith tests silver.

  • vv5–6 the lappers — v5 describes lapping with his tongue, as a dog laps; v6 counts those who lapped putting their hand to their mouth. The Hebrew and the Greek agree, and the two descriptions are not harmonized. What matters to the story is the number: three hundred.

  • v13 "a round loaf of barley bread" — a loaf of bread is no weapon. The dream shows a small, ordinary thing flattening the tent of a vast army, and the Midianite who hears it names it at once: the sword of Gideon.

  • v15 "its interpretation" — shivro, its breaking. Shever is the plain word for a break, and only here is it used for the meaning of a dream: the dream is cracked open. Four verses later, the jars are broken.

  • v16 "torches inside the jars" — lappidim, the same word as in Lappidoth (4:4). The clay hides the light until the jars are smashed.

  • v22 "the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow" — Israel's three hundred hold horns and torches, not swords. The swords in the story are Midian's, turned on each other.

  • v25 "Oreb and Zeeb" — Raven and Wolf. Zeeb dies at a winepress, where Gideon was first found hiding (6:11). Isaiah 10:26 remembers the striking of Midian at the rock of Oreb.

chapters.title: Gideon's Pursuit, and the Ephod
chapters.html:
Judges 8

Ephraim

1The men of Ephraim said to him, "What is this you have done to us, not calling us when you went to fight against Midian?" They quarreled with him fiercely.

2He said to them, "What have I done now compared with you? Is not the gleaning of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?

3God gave the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, into your hand. What have I been able to do compared with you?" When he said this, their anger against him subsided.

Succoth and Penuel

4Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men who were with him, exhausted but still pursuing.

5He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."

6The officials of Succoth said, "Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?"

7Gideon said, "For that, when the LORD has given Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers."

8He went up from there to Penuel and spoke to them the same way, and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered.

9He said also to the men of Penuel, "When I come back in peace, I will tear down this tower."

10Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their army with them, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of the whole army of the sons of the east; for a hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword had fallen.

11Gideon went up by the road of the tent-dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the army while the army was off guard.

12Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued them. He captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and threw the whole army into terror.

13Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres.

14He caught a young man of the men of Succoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the officials of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.

15He came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your exhausted men?'"

16He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth a lesson.

17He tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.

Zebah and Zalmunna

18Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Where are the men you killed at Tabor?" They said, "They were like you, every one of them; each looked like the son of a king."

19He said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you."

20He said to Jether his firstborn, "Up, kill them!" But the boy did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a boy.

21Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Get up yourself and strike us down, for as the man is, so is his strength." So Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.

The Ephod

22The men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us, you and your son and your son's son also, for you have saved us from the hand of Midian."

23Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."

24Gideon said to them, "Let me make a request of you: every one of you give me an earring from his spoil." For they had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.

25They said, "We will give them." They spread out a cloak, and every man threw on it an earring from his spoil.

26The weight of the gold earrings that he requested was a thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescent ornaments, the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that were on the necks of their camels.

27Gideon made an ephod of it and set it up in his city, in Ophrah. All Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.

28So Midian was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they did not raise their heads again. The land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.

Gideon's Death

29Jerubbaal son of Joash went and lived in his own house.

30Gideon had seventy sons, his own offspring, for he had many wives.

31His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.

32Gideon son of Joash died at a good gray age and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

33And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the sons of Israel turned again and prostituted themselves after the Baals, and made Baal-berith their god.

34The sons of Israel did not remember the LORD their God, who had delivered them from the hand of all their enemies all around,

35and they did not show loyal love to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, for all the good he had done for Israel.

Notes

  • v2 "Is not the gleaning of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?" — olelot, the grapes left on the vine after the harvest. Gideon answers Ephraim's anger with a proverb: their leftovers, the two princes they caught, outweigh his whole clan's harvest. Their anger subsided is rafetah rucham, their spirit sank.

  • vv6, 15 "Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand?" — ha-khaf, the palm. The officials of Succoth will not stake bread on a victory not yet won.

  • vv7, 16 "I will thresh your flesh… he taught the men of Succoth a lesson" — in v7 Gideon promises to thresh, dashti; in v16 the Hebrew has va-yoda, he made them know. The Greek has he threshed in both, reading va-yadosh, one letter different, which is what Gideon promised. The text follows the Hebrew.

  • v12 "threw the whole army into terror" — hecherid, from charad, to tremble, the root of the spring of Harod where Gideon sent home the ones who trembled (7:1, 3). Now the enemy trembles.

  • vv18–19 "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother" — the battle at Tabor is not told anywhere. Gideon's last pursuit turns out to be the avenging of his own brothers.

  • vv22–23 "Rule over us… The LORD will rule over you" — the first time Israel asks for a ruling house, a father, a son and a grandson. Gideon refuses in the words Samuel will hear from the LORD: they have rejected Me from being king over them (1 Samuel 8:7). Yet in v31 he names a son Abimelech, my father is king, and chapter 9 follows him.

  • v24 "because they were Ishmaelites" — the Midianites are called Ishmaelites, as in the story of Joseph, where Midianite traders and Ishmaelites are named together as the ones who carried him to Egypt (Genesis 37:25, 28).

  • v27 "Gideon made an ephod of it" — the ephod is the high priest's garment (Exodus 28:4), which carried the breastpiece with the Urim and the Thummim (28:30), used for asking the LORD's will. Gideon's gold one becomes an object of worship in his own town, and a snare (moqesh, as in 2:3) to his house.

  • v32 "at a good gray age" — be-seivah tovah, the words said of Abraham (Genesis 15:15, 25:8).

  • v33 "Baal-berith" — Baal of the covenant. The people who would not keep the LORD's covenant make a god of the word. His temple stands at Shechem (9:4).

Gideon went up by the road of the tent-dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the army while the army was off guard.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued them. He captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and threw the whole army into terror.
Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres.
He caught a young man of the men of Succoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the officials of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.

He came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your exhausted men?'"
He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth a lesson.
He tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
Zebah and Zalmunna
Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Where are the men you killed at Tabor?" They said, "They were like you, every one of them; each looked like the son of a king."
He said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you."
He said to Jether his firstborn, "Up, kill them!" But the boy did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a boy.

Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Get up yourself and strike us down, for as the man is, so is his strength." So Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
The Ephod
The men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us, you and your son and your son's son also, for you have saved us from the hand of Midian."
Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."
Gideon said to them, "Let me make a request of you: every one of you give me an earring from his spoil." For they had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.
They said, "We will give them." They spread out a cloak, and every man threw on it an earring from his spoil.

The weight of the gold earrings that he requested was a thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescent ornaments, the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that were on the necks of their camels.
Gideon made an ephod of it and set it up in his city, in Ophrah. All Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.
So Midian was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they did not raise their heads again. The land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.
Gideon's Death
Jerubbaal son of Joash went and lived in his own house.
Gideon had seventy sons, his own offspring, for he had many wives.
His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
Gideon son of Joash died at a good gray age and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the sons of Israel turned again and prostituted themselves after the Baals, and made Baal-berith their god.
The sons of Israel did not remember the LORD their God, who had delivered them from the hand of all their enemies all around,
and they did not show loyal love to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, for all the good he had done for Israel.
